title: DeMix: Debugging Training Data with Mixed Data Error Types by Investigating Influence Vectors

problem.claim: Real-world training datasets contain mixed error types, including label errors, feature errors, and spurious correlations.

gap.claim: Existing data cleaning and attribution methods do not adequately detect erroneous samples while identifying their specific error types for targeted repair.

contributions.claim: DeMix simultaneously diagnoses erroneous training samples and their error types.
DeMix uses influence vectors and a multi-label classifier to predict error types from each sample's effects on validation predictions.
DeMix introduces intervention-based learning to capture invariant rationales specific to each error type.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe DeMix as a novel framework for simultaneous diagnosis of erroneous samples and their error types.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that evaluations across 11 tasks in tabular prediction, recommendation systems, and LLM alignment show DeMix significantly outperforms state-of-the-art approaches.
The authors report a 22.61% improvement in data-debugging F1-score and a 9.32% gain in task-model performance after data repair.
The authors state that code is available in a public GitHub repository.

narrative_sequence.summary: High-quality training data is important for successful machine learning models.
Real-world datasets contain multiple error types, creating a need for detection and type-specific diagnosis.
DeMix represents sample effects with influence vectors and predicts error types through multi-label classification with intervention-based learning.
The authors report evaluations across 11 tasks with improvements in debugging F1-score and task-model performance after repair.
The authors provide a code repository link.

source_observation.claim: Different error types are described as producing distinct patterns in model behavior, which can be represented through influence vectors across validation samples.

interpretation.claim: Model-behavior effects may provide a basis for distinguishing heterogeneous training-data errors.

application.claim: Training-data debugging systems could analyze per-sample influence patterns when error-type-specific repair is needed.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether influence vectors remain discriminative across datasets, models, or error types beyond the reported tasks.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the 11 tasks, datasets, models, baselines, or evaluation protocol.
The abstract does not define the exact error taxonomy or repair procedure.
The abstract does not provide statistical uncertainty, ablations, or implementation details.
